question:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1\\2 & 1 & 3\\3 & -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Evaluate $|A|$ by expanding along the first row.

(b) Evaluate $|A|$ again by expanding along the second column.

(c) Compare the results and justify whether the value of a determinant depends on the row or column selected for expansion.
explanation:
(a)
Expanding along the first row,
$$|A|=1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3\\-1 & 2\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3\\3 & 2\end{vmatrix}+(-1)\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & -1\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A|=1(2+3)-2(4-9)-1(-2-3)$$
$$|A|=5+10+5=20$$

(b)
Expanding along the second column, the signs of the cofactors are negative, positive and negative:
$$|A|=-2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3\\3 & 2\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}1 & -1\\3 & 2\end{vmatrix}-(-1)\begin{vmatrix}1 & -1\\2 & 3\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A|=-2(4-9)+(2+3)+(3+2)$$
$$|A|=10+5+5=20$$

(c)
Both expansions give
$$|A|=20$$
Therefore, the value of a determinant is independent of the row or column chosen for expansion, provided the signs and corresponding minors are used correctly.

options.A:
(a) First-row expansion gives $|A|=20$
(b) Second-column expansion also gives $|A|=20$
(c) The determinant is independent of the row or column chosen for expansion
options.B:
(a) First-row expansion gives $|A|=-20$
(b) Second-column expansion gives $|A|=20$
(c) The determinant depends on the chosen row or column
options.C:
(a) First-row expansion gives $|A|=20$
(b) Second-column expansion gives $|A|=-20$
(c) Expansion along a column reverses the sign
options.D:
(a) First-row expansion gives $|A|=10$
(b) Second-column expansion gives $|A|=10$
(c) The value depends only on the number of non-zero entries
